n1.point: Complainant is Optimum Communications Services, Inc. (OCS), a Delaware corporation based in Jersey City, New Jersey, which has been developing and marketing technologies protected by the asserted patents since 2001 through its predecessor Optimum Communications Technologies, Inc.
n1.quote: Complainant Optimum Communications Services, Inc. ("OCS") is a Delaware corporation having a principal place of business at 344 Grove Street #242, Jersey City, NJ 07302. Since 2001

n10.point: The complainant's own products are xPON standards based FTTx (fiber-to-the-home/premises) products and services, including design, engineering, installation, testing, and provisioning for customers, with authorized use by municipal FTTH networks.
n10.quote: domestic industry participants' xPON standards based products and services are exploiting the asserted patents. The primary technology standard used for US FTTx is xPON

n100.point: The Commission vote for the final determination took place on April 25, 2025.
n100.quote: The Commission vote for this determination took place on April 25, 2025.

n11.point: U.S. Patent No. 7,558,260 (the '260 patent) is directed to a self-optimizing digital communications network using dynamic frame-slot assignment among source nodes, filed March 7, 2003, issued July 7, 2009, expiring January 10, 2026.
n11.quote: The '260 patent is directed to a self-optimizing digital communications network for transporting data among a set of nodes, such as routers, switches or terminal equipment, based on multi-source-node data transport channels, which have a framed carrier signal, and on which frame-slots are dynamically assigned

n12.point: U.S. Patent No. 7,333,511 (the '511 patent) is directed to a communications network for transporting data packets among L2/L3 nodes based on dynamically L1-channelizable multi-source buses, filed August 29, 2002, issued February 19, 2008, expiring July 30, 2025.
n12.quote: The '511 patent is directed to a communications network for transporting data packets among L2/L3 nodes based on dynamically L1-channelizable multi-source buses (Abstract), was filed on August 29, 2002 by inventor Mark Sandstrom, was issued on February 19, 2008

n13.point: The complainant alleges that the '260 patent claims 1 and 3, and the '511 patent claims 1 and 12-14 are infringed by the accused products.
n13.quote: Complainant asserts that the Proposed Respondents' accused products practice at least claims 1 and 3 of the '260 patent as well as at least claims 1 and 12-14 of the '511 patent.

n14.point: Both asserted patents are assigned to Complainant through chains of assignments, with the '260 patent assigned from inventor to Optimum Communications Technologies, Inc., then to Optimum Communications Services, Inc., Alberta, then to Optimum Communications Services, Inc., Delaware.
n14.quote: via the assignment 013999/0528 recorded on September 24, 2003, the underlying application 10/382729 was assigned by the inventor to Optimum Communications Technologies, Inc.

n15.point: Neither the '260 patent nor the '511 patent has been licensed.
n15.quote: The '260 patent has not been licensed.

n16.point: The accused products are imported through online marketplaces such as made-in-china.com, alibaba.com, and aliexpress.com, with prices quoted in U.S. dollars and U.S. shipping available as an option.
n16.quote: At the made-in-china.com online market place, GPON standard OLT and ONU products are offered from large number of China-based suppliers with prices quoted in U.S. dollars and the U.S. being available as the shipping destination

n17.point: On made-in-china.com alone, there are 192 manufacturers and suppliers with 576 GPON OLT products and 201 manufacturers and suppliers with 603 GPON ONU products listed for importation.
n17.quote: Per above, at this online market place alone, for GPON OLT imports, there were " Total 192 manufacturers & suppliers found with 576 products ".

n18.point: The respondents confirm capability to ship products to the United States; Softel confirmed via online chat on November 5, 2023 that they ship xPON products to US addresses, and DAYTAI confirmed they ship OLT and ONUs to the USA.
n18.quote: Via online chat at the made-in-china.com on November 5, 2023, Softel's representative confirmed that they do ship their xPON products a shipping address in the US

n19.point: The respondents price their products in U.S. dollars, facilitating payment from U.S. customers.
n19.quote: Softel prices and takes payments for their xPON products in U.S. Dollars

n2.point: Mark Sandstrom is the President of Complainant and the named inventor on each of the asserted patents.
n2.quote: Complainant's President, Mark Sandstrom, is the named inventor on each of the asserted patents.

n20.point: The complainant alleges that the accused xPON products implement the GPON standard, which per claim charts in Exhibit VII requires OLT and ONU equipment to have features recited in at least the first claim of each asserted patent.
n20.quote: Each of the proposed respondents' xPON OLT and ONU/ONT product imports, per below, are characterized as supporting at least the base GPON standard for xPONs, which per Exhibit VII, requires a compliant OLT and ONU equipment to have the features recited in at least the first claim

n21.point: The complainant alleges that because xPON standards require both OLT and ONU equipment working together, any importation of either type of equipment results in implementation of an xPON standard that infringes the asserted patents.
n21.quote: There is no conceivable usage of either OLT or ONU equipment apart from each others, as the xPON standards, and practical operation of any passive optical networks, e.g. for FTTx deployments, require presence of each type of equipment

n22.point: The claim charts in Exhibit VII apply asserted patent claims to GPON (ITU-T G.984.3), 10GPON (G.987.3), TWDM-PON (G.989.3), and EPON/10G-EPON (IEEE 802.3ah/802.3av) standards.
n22.quote: Exhibits per below include claim charts that apply several claims of the asserted patents to certain network protocol standards

n23.point: A domestic industry exists relating to xPON standard products and services, with domestic industry participants selling, distributing and supporting products protected by the asserted patents.
n23.quote: Domestic industry participants sell, distribute and support products and services that are protected by one or more claims (e.g., first claim) of each of the asserted patents.

n24.point: The primary technology standard for U.S. FTTx is xPON, and GPON is the most popular version of FTTH PONs used in the domestic industry.
n24.quote: The primary technology standard used for US FTTx is xPON, e.g. per: * https://www.eff.org/wp/case-fiber-home-today-why-fiber-superior-medium-21st-century-broadband: The most common FTTH architecture is the Passive Optical Network (PON)

n25.point: The complainant has authorized usage of the asserted patents for xPON based municipal FTTH networks, specifically EPB Fiber Optics in Chattanooga, Tennessee, which provides GPON-based services to 126,086 customers.
n25.quote: Complainant has authorized the usage of the asserted patents for certain xPON based municipal FTTH networks, as elaborated in the Confidential Economic Prong Declaration (Exhibit I (C)). Information regarding such a municipal FTTx network based on xPON standards

n26.point: The EPB Chattanooga GPON network represents significant investment of approximately US$220 million to build, with 82 OLTs, 91 miles of transport fiber, 802 miles of feeder fiber, 3,365 miles of distribution fiber, and 4,300+ miles of drop fiber.
n26.quote: Per https://communitynets.org/content/study-finds-chattanooga-fiber-network-10-year-roi-269-billion, "It cost approximately $220 million to build the network"

n27.point: The complainant calculates domestic industry investment in xPON equipment for the EPB network alone at over US$10 million in equipment costs (excluding engineering, installation and OAM costs), using typical ONU to OLT ratios and equipment prices from respondents.
n27.quote: the cost for the xPON OLT and ONU products protected by the asserted patents for the EPB FTTx network of 126,086 fiber optics has been at least 126086*($35+$1450/32) i.e. more than $10M

n28.point: The complainant requests a permanent general exclusion order prohibiting entry into the United States of accused xPON products that infringe one or more claims of the asserted patents.
n28.quote: Issue a permanent general exclusion order, pursuant to Section 337(d), forbidding entry into the United States of the accused xPON products that infringe one or more claims of the asserted patents

n29.point: The complainant requests a permanent cease and desist order directing any parties to cease importing, selling, offering for sale, distributing, warehousing, testing, using, programming, repairing, maintaining, demonstrating, promoting, marketing or advertising accused xPON products that infringe the asserted patents.
n29.quote: Issue a permanent order, pursuant to Section 337(f), directing any parties to cease and desist from the importing, sale for importing, sale after importing, offering for sale, distributing, warehousing, transferring, testing, using, programming

n3.point: Proposed respondent Hangzhou Softel Optic Co., Ltd. (Softel) is a Chinese trading company with annual output value of US$2.5 Million - US$5 Million and main markets in North America that sells GPON OLT and ONU equipment.
n3.quote: Hangzhou Softel Optic Co., Ltd., (Softel), with per Section VII "Annual Output Value: US$2.5 Million - US$5 Million" (noting that the importer themselves reports this in U.S. dollars)

n30.point: The complainant requests a target date of no more than sixteen months for the investigation.
n30.quote: Set a target date of no more than sixteen months

n31.point: The investigation concerns certain OLT and ONU/ONT equipment for GPON and successor standard based Passive Optical Networks (xPONs), including subassemblies thereof, supporting Dynamic Bandwidth Assignment (DBA) that infringe one or more claims of the asserted patents.
n31.quote: certain OLT and ONU/ONT equipment for GPON and successor standard based Passive Optical Networks (xPONs), including subassemblies thereof, supporting Dynamic Bandwidth Assignment (DBA)

n32.point: The complainant affirms that there is no other past or present domestic or foreign litigation concerning the asserted patents.
n32.quote: In accordance with Commission Rule 210.12(a)(5), Complainant affirms that there is no other past or present domestic or foreign litigation concerning the asserted patents.

n33.point: The complainant seeks a general exclusion order on the grounds that there is a pattern of violation and it is difficult to track and identify the brands and sources of infringing products due to hundreds of corporate entities offering xPON equipment under variable importer/brand names via online marketplaces.
n33.quote: Complainant thus submits that there is a pattern of violation of the Section 337, and it is difficult to track and identify the brands and sources of infringing products

n34.point: Customization services such as custom product labeling are available for the accused products, facilitating importing of infringing articles under variable importer and brand names.
n34.quote: customization, e.g. product labeling per buyer's requests, is available for at least each of the proposed respondents' xPON standard equipment identified above

n35.point: Hundreds of subassembly products for xPON equipment such as populated circuit boards are available for importation via online marketplaces, facilitating circumvention through variable importer names.
n35.quote: several hundreds of subassembly products for xPON equipment, such as circuit boards populated with the componentry implementing digital and opto-electronic functionality for the xPON standards, are available

n36.point: It is not practically feasible to identify any significant portion of the several hundred corporate entities under whose brand names unlicensed xPON equipment has been, is, or could be imported.
n36.quote: In these circumstances, it is not practically feasible to identify any significant portion of the possibly several hundreds of corporate entities under whose brand names unlicensed xPON equipment have been, are, or could be, imported.

n37.point: New supplier brands with capability to take and fill orders internationally can be set up quickly due to standardization of xPON product functionality and the availability of online marketplaces for low-cost imports.
n37.quote: The standardization of the xPON product functionality and the online market places (e.g. per above) for the low-cost xPON product imports have created circumstances where new supplier brands, with capability to take and fill orders internationally, can be set up quickly.

n38.point: The complaint is verified by Mark Sandstrom, President of Complainant, filed November 10, 2023 and supplemented November 21, 2023.
n38.quote: Dated: November 10, 2023     Respectfully submitted: _____________________________ Mark Sandstrom, President Optimum Communications Services, Inc.

n39.point: Complainant's predecessor, Optimum Communications Technologies, Inc., had a place of business at 701 Taylor Street #206, San Francisco, California, where the inventions were originally developed.
n39.quote: beginning with OCS' corporate predecessor, Optimum Communications Technologies, Inc., a Delaware corporation, which had a place of business at 701 Taylor Street #206, San Francisco, CA 94108

n4.point: Proposed respondent Hangzhou DAYTAI Network Technologies Co., Ltd. (DAYTAI) is a Chinese supplier with annual output value of US$10 Million - US$50 Million and main markets in North America that supplies GPON standard OLT and ONU equipment.
n4.quote: Hangzhou DAYTAI Network Technologies Co., Ltd. (DAYTAI), with per Section III. B., " Annual Output Value: US$10 Million - US$50 Million " (noting that the importer themselves reports this in U.S. dollars)

n40.point: The complainant affirms that there are no foreign patents or patent applications corresponding to the asserted patents.
n40.quote: In accordance with Commission Rule 210.12(a)(9)(v), Complainant affirms that there are no foreign patents or patent applications corresponding to the asserted patents

n41.point: The identified respondents leverage international trading capabilities of online marketplaces such as made-in-china.com, alibaba.com, and aliexpress.com to offer and sell xPON products.
n41.quote: Suppliers, such as the proposed respondents per above, leverage international trading capabilities of online marketplaces such as https://www.made-in-china.com/

n42.point: The complainant is Optimum Communications Services, Inc. of Jersey City, New Jersey.
n42.quote: Optimum Communications Services, Inc. 344 Grove Street #242, Jersey City, NJ 07302

n43.point: The respondents are Hangzhou Softel Optic Co., Ltd., Hangzhou DAYTAI Network Technologies Co., Ltd., and Hangzhou Sumlo Industrial Co., Ltd., all located in China.
n43.quote: Hangzhou Softel Optic Co., Ltd. 708 709 Haiwei Building, 101 Binkang Road, Binjiang District, Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China 310051

n44.point: The investigation covers infringement of claims 1 and 12-14 of U.S. Patent No. 7,333,511 and claims 1 and 3 of U.S. Patent No. 7,558,260.
n44.quote: claims 1 and 12-14 of the '511 patent and claims 1 and 3 of the '260 patent

n45.point: The accused products are optical line termination (OLT) and optical network unit/terminal (ONU/ONT) equipment conforming to passive optical network standards including G-PON, 10GPON/XGS-PON, TWDM-PON/NG-PON2, and IEEE 802.3ah (EPON) and 802.3av (10G-EPON).
n45.quote: optical line termination (OLT) and optical network unit/terminal (ONU/ONT) equipment that conform to passive optical network standards of ITU-T Recommendation series G.984.x for Gigabit-capable Passive Optical Network (G-PON) and its successor standards, including 10GPON/XGS-PON (ITU-T Rec. G.987.3) and TWDM-PON/NG-PON2 (ITU-T Rec. G.989.3) as well as IEEE 802.3ah (EPON) and 802.3av (10G-EPON)

n46.point: The Office of Unfair Import Investigations is named as a party to the investigation.
n46.quote: The Office of Unfair Import Investigations, U.S. International Trade Commission, 500 E Street, S.W., Suite 401, Washington, D.C. 20436

n47.point: The complainant requests a general exclusion order or in the alternative a limited exclusion order, and a cease and desist order.
n47.quote: issue a general exclusion order, or in the alternative a limited exclusion, and a cease and desist order

n48.point: Complainant Optimum Communications Services, Inc. is a Delaware corporation based in Jersey City, New Jersey; the three named respondents are Hangzhou Sumlo Industrial Co., Ltd., Hangzhou DAYTAI Network Technologies Co., Ltd., and Hangzhou Softel Optic Co., Ltd., all Chinese companies.
n48.quote: Optimum Communications Services, Inc. is a Delaware corporation having a principal place of business in Jersey City, New Jersey.

n49.point: Optimum asserts claims 1 and 12-14 of U.S. Patent No. 7,333,511 (the '511 patent) and claims 1 and 3 of U.S. Patent No. 7,558,260 (the '260 patent).
n49.quote: whether there is a violation of subsection (a)(1)(B) of section 337 in the importation into the United States, the sale for importation, or the sale within the United States after importation of certain products identified in paragraph (2) by reason of infringement of one or more of claims 1 and 12–14 of [U.S. Patent No. 7,333,511] and claims 1 and 3 of [U.S. Patent No. 7,558,260]

n5.point: Proposed respondent Hangzhou Sumlo Industrial Co., Ltd. (Sumlo) is a Chinese manufacturer/trading company with annual export revenue exceeding US$100 million that offers GPON OLT and ONU equipment.
n5.quote: Hangzhou Sumlo Industrial Co., Ltd. (Sumlo), with per section VII "Annual Export Revenue: >100 million USD" (noting that the importer themselves reports this in U.S. dollars)

n50.point: The accused products are described as optical line termination (OLT) and optical network unit/terminal (ONU/ONT) equipment that conform to passive optical network standards including ITU-T Recommendation series G.984.x for Gigabit-capable Passive Optical Network (G-PON), 10GPON/XGS-PON, TWDM-PON/NG-PON2, IEEE 802.3ah (EPON), and 802.3av (10G-EPON).
n50.quote: optical line termination (OLT) and optical network unit/terminal (ONU/ONT) equipment that conform to passive optical network standards of ITU-T Recommendation series G.984.x for Gigabit -capable Passive Optical Network (G -PON) and its successor standards

n51.point: Optimum has not specifically identified any accused products by name, model number, or manufacturer, despite repeated Staff requests to do so.
n51.quote: Optimum has not specifically identified any accused products from the three named respondents that allegedly infringe any of the asserted claims of either asserted patent despite repeated requests to do so by the Staff.

n52.point: The ALJ found that Optimum has not provided substantial, reliable, and probative evidence establishing infringement of any of the asserted claims because Optimum practices the standard rather than identifying specific infringing products.
n52.quote: Instead of identifying specific accused products, Optimum contends that the practice of certain standards infringes the asserted claims.

n53.point: Optimum abandoned its infringement allegations regarding IEEE 802.3ah (EPON) and 802.3av (10G-EPON) standards by not presenting them in its hearing brief, limiting its allegations to ITU Recommendations G.984.3, G.987.3, and G.989.3.
n53.quote: By not presenting any infringement contentions as to the IEEE 802.3ah (EPON) or 802.3av (10G-EPON) standards (or as to CX-0019 or CX-0020) in its hearing brief, Optimum has abandoned any such contentions.

n54.point: The ALJ found that Optimum has not satisfied the technical prong of the domestic industry requirement because it has not identified specific domestic industry products that practice the asserted claims.
n54.quote: Based on the contentions in its hearing brief, Optimum has limited its allegations of domestic industry to those it made in asserting infringement, namely ITU Recommendations G.984.3, G.987.3, and G.989.3.

n55.point: The ALJ found that EPB did not become a licensee of the asserted patents until June 12, 2024, well after the complaint was filed on November 14, 2023, and therefore EPB's expenditures cannot be used to demonstrate an economic domestic industry.
n55.quote: The evidence supports, at most, that EPB became a licensee to the asserted patents well after this investigation was instituted and indeed after briefing was completed.

n56.point: The ALJ found that Optimum's October 16, 2023 authorization letter to EPB did not create a license because it explicitly stated that Optimum was not granting a royalty-free license to practice any of its patents for unlimited purposes.
n56.quote: this letter should not be understood to indicate that OCS is granting a royalty-free license to practice any of its patents for unlimited purposes

n57.point: The ALJ found that the economic prong of the domestic industry requirement has not been satisfied because Optimum failed to provide a quantitative analysis of EPB's investments and offered only unsubstantiated qualitative assertions about regional and national significance.
n57.quote: A quantitative analysis is required for satisfaction of the economic prong of the domestic industry requirement.

n58.point: The ALJ found that the importation requirement has not been satisfied in the conclusions of law.
n58.quote: 2. The importation requirement has not been satisfied.

n59.point: The Staff did not challenge the validity of any of the asserted claims, and as a result there has been no showing that any of the asserted claims is invalid.
n59.quote: The Staff does not challenge the validity of any of the asserted claims. Staff Br. at 44. As a result, there has been no showing that any of the asserted claims is invalid.

n6.point: The patented technology relates to Dynamic Bandwidth Assignment (DBA) capability, which improves cost-efficiency of fiber-optic network connectivity by intelligently sharing broadband bandwidth among multiple subscribers so each gets at least their subscribed amount and usually more.
n6.quote: The asserted patents claim inventions that improve cost-efficiency of fiberoptic network connectivity. More specifically, the asserted claims enable intelligent dynamic sharing of broadband Internet access bandwidth among multiple subscribers

n60.point: The ALJ's initial determination is that a violation of Section 337 of the Tariff Act has not occurred by the importation, sale for importation, or sale within the United States after importation of products that infringe U.S. Patent No. 7,558,260 or U.S. Patent No. 7,333,511.
n60.quote: It is my initial determination that a violation of section 337 of the Tariff Act, as amended, has not occurred by the importation into the United States, the sale for importation, or the sale within the United States after importation of products that infringe U.S. Patent No. 7,558,260 and U.S. Patent No. 7,333,511.

n61.point: Because no violation of Section 337 was found, the ALJ recommends no limited exclusion orders, no cease and desist orders, and no general exclusion orders issue.
n61.quote: I recommend that no limited exclusion orders issue against any of the defaulted respondents.

n62.point: The ALJ notes that even if a violation were found, Optimum seeks a general exclusion order barring entry into the United States of articles from any source that infringe the asserted claims.
n62.quote: Optimum seeks a general exclusion order barring entry into the United States of articles, regardless of source, that infringe claims 1 and 12-14 of the '511 patent or claims 1 and 3 of the 260 patent.

n63.point: The ALJ recommends a 0% bond because Optimum has not demonstrated that it would be injured if a bond is not set, noting that Optimum has not sold any physical products and has no evidence of ever licensing the asserted patents for royalties.
n63.quote: Because Optimum has failed to demonstrate the necessity of a bond, it is my recommendation that the Commission, in the event it finds a violation of section 337 has occurred, set a 0% bond for any importations of infringing products during the Presidential review period.

n64.point: The ALJ found that the Commission lacks statutory authority with respect to the investigation because Optimum is not the owner or exclusive licensee of the asserted patents.
n64.quote: 1. The Commission lacks statutory authority with respect to this investigation because Optimum is not the owner or exclusive licensee of the asserted patents.

n65.point: After the investigation was instituted, Optimum assigned the asserted patents to Mark Sandstrom on July 18, 2024, and Sandstrom then reassigned them to Optimum on August 27, 2024; the ALJ found these post-institution assignments rendered Optimum's standing questionable.
n65.quote: That document, dated July 18, 2024 (after institution of this investigation), states that Optimum Communication Services, Inc. "assign[ed] unto Mark Sandstrom" several patents, including the asserted patents.

n66.point: Xenogenic Development LLC moved to intervene in the investigation, claiming it owns the asserted patents; the ALJ granted Xenogenic limited intervenor status for purposes of addressing ownership-related issues in the event of Commission review.
n66.quote: Proposed intervenor Xenogenic contends that it owns the asserted patents and moved to intervene on that basis.

n67.point: All three named respondents—Sumlo, DAYTAI, and Softel—were found in default by initial determination on April 10, 2024.
n67.quote: I issued an initial determination finding all three named respondents in default. Order No. 12 (initial determination) (Apr. 10, 2024) (EDIS Doc. ID 818209), unreviewed by, Comm'n Notice (May 9, 2024) (EDIS Doc. ID 821098).

n68.point: Optimum filed a motion for the admission of CX-0058C, an exhibit containing emails between Optimum and EPB dated through June 20, 2024, in which EPB confirmed licensee status; the motion was granted after briefing was completed.
n68.quote: After briefing was concluded, Optimum filed a motion for the admission of CX-0058C. The Staff did not oppose, and the motion was granted.

n69.point: After the investigation was instituted, Mark Sandstrom filed a Declaratory Judgment action in the U.S. District Court for the District of Minnesota against Ericsson, asserting that he owns the patents asserted in this investigation.
n69.quote: affer this investigation was instituted, Mr. Sandstrom, the president of Optimum, filed a Declaratory Judgment action in the U.S. District Court for the District of Minnesota seeking a declaration that Defendants Ericsson Inc. and Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson require a license for certain patents, including the '260 and '511 patents asserted in this investigation.

n7.point: The DBA technology is utilized in passive optical network (xPON) standards including GPON (ITU-T G.984.x), 10GPON/XGS-PON (G.987.3), TWDM-PON/NG-PON2 (G.989.3), and EPON/10G-EPON (IEEE 802.3ah/802.3av).
n7.quote: passive optical network equipment compliant with the ITU-T standard for Gigabit-capable Passive Optical Network (GPON), i.e. the Recommendation series G.984.x, specifically, the upstream direction Dynamic Bandwidth Assignment (DBA) mechanism

n70.point: The investigation was instituted to determine whether there is a violation of Section 337(a)(1)(B) based on infringement of the asserted patent claims and whether a domestic industry exists as required by Section 337(a)(2).
n70.quote: The Commission instituted this investigation to determine: whether there is a violation of subsection (a)(1)(B) of section 337 in the importation into the United States, the sale for importation, or the sale within the United States after importation of certain products

n71.point: The central issue is whether the practice of certain ITU and IEEE standards infringes the asserted claims, which the ALJ found Optimum failed to establish because it did not identify specific products or explain how the standards implement the claimed inventions.
n71.quote: Instead of identifying specific accused products, Optimum contends that the practice of certain standards infringes the asserted claims.

n72.point: The ALJ decided that Ground Rule 11.2 applied, requiring parties to detail all contentions in pre-hearing briefs; Optimum's failure to address IEEE standards in its hearing brief resulted in abandonment of those claims.
n72.quote: By not presenting any infringement contentions as to the IEEE 802.3ah (EPON) or 802.3av (10G-EPON) standards (or as to CX-0019 or CX-0020) in its hearing brief, Optimum has abandoned any such contentions.

n73.point: Optimum proceeded pro se in this investigation, and the Staff and defaulted respondents opposed many of Optimum's contentions regarding infringement, domestic industry, and ownership.
n73.quote: Optimum is proceeding pro se in this investigation.

n74.point: Optimum Communications Services, Inc. of Jersey City, New Jersey is the complainant; the respondents are Hangzhou Softel Optic Co., Ltd., Hangzhou DAYTAI Network Technologies Co., Ltd., and Hangzhou Sumlo Industrial Co., Ltd., all of Hangzhou, China; and the Office of Unfair Import Investigations is also a party.
n74.quote: Optimum Communications Services, Inc. of Jersey City, New Jersey ("Optimum"). 88 FR 90200-01 (Dec. 29, 2023). The complaint, as supplemented, alleges violations of section 337 of the Tariff Act of 1930

n75.point: The complaint alleges violations of Section 337 based on infringement of claims 1 and 12-14 of U.S. Patent No. 7,333,511 ('511 patent) and claims 1 and 3 of U.S. Patent No. 7,558,260 ('260 patent) by certain passive optical network equipment.
n75.quote: based upon the importation into the United States, the sale for importation, and the sale in the United States after importation of certain passive optical network equipment by reason of the infringement of certain claims of U.S. Patent Nos. 7,333,511

n76.point: The complaint alleges that a domestic industry exists in the asserted patents.
n76.quote: The complaint further alleges that a domestic industry exists.

about.text: The complainant is Optimum Communications Services, Inc. (OCS), a Delaware corporation based in Jersey City, New Jersey, which has developed and marketed technology in this field since 2001 through a predecessor company. Mark Sandstrom, OCS's President, is the named inventor on both patents asserted in the case. The three named respondents are Hangzhou Softel Optic Co., Ltd., Hangzhou DAYTAI Network Technologies Co., Ltd., and Hangzhou Sumlo Industrial Co., Ltd., all Chinese companies that sell GPON optical line termination (OLT) and optical network unit/terminal (ONU/ONT) equipment with markets in North America.

The technology at issue is Dynamic Bandwidth Assignment (DBA), a way of sharing fiber-optic bandwidth among many subscribers so each gets at least a guaranteed amount and usually more. DBA is used in passive optical network (xPON) standards such as GPON, 10GPON/XGS-PON, TWDM-PON/NG-PON2, and EPON/10G-EPON. The complaint asserted two patents: U.S. Patent No. 7,558,260 (the '260 patent), covering a self-optimizing communications network using dynamic frame-slot assignment, and U.S. Patent No. 7,333,511 (the '511 patent), covering a communications network that transports data using dynamically channelizable multi-source buses. The Commission instituted the investigation to determine whether there was a violation of Section 337 based on infringement of claims 1 and 3 of the '260 patent and claims 1 and 12-14 of the '511 patent, and whether a domestic industry existed as required by the statute, with the Office of Unfair Import Investigations named as a party representing the public interest.

allegations.text: OCS alleged that the respondents' GPON OLT and ONU equipment, sold through online marketplaces such as made-in-china.com, alibaba.com, and aliexpress.com and priced in U.S. dollars, was imported into or sold within the United States, since the respondents confirmed they could and did ship xPON products to U.S. addresses. OCS alleged that because xPON standards require OLT and ONU equipment to work together, importation of either type results in implementation of an xPON standard that infringes the asserted patents, applying claim charts against GPON, 10GPON, TWDM-PON, and EPON/10G-EPON standards.

For domestic industry -- the complainant's U.S. investment tied to the patented technology that Section 337 requires -- OCS pointed to authorized use of xPON standard products and services by municipal fiber-to-the-home networks, particularly EPB Fiber Optics in Chattanooga, Tennessee, which OCS said had invested roughly $220 million building its GPON network and served over 126,000 customers, with OCS calculating domestic industry equipment investment at over $10 million.

OCS asked for a general exclusion order, a Commission order barring importation of infringing products by any source rather than just named respondents, on the theory that hundreds of corporate entities sell interchangeable xPON equipment under variable brand names via online marketplaces, making it impracticable to identify infringers individually; alternatively it sought a limited exclusion order against the named respondents. OCS also requested a cease and desist order barring further sale, distribution, and marketing of infringing products within the United States, and asked for a target date of no more than sixteen months.

decisions.text: In the final initial determination (ID) issued December 19, 2024, the ALJ found that no violation of Section 337 had occurred as to either the '511 patent or the '260 patent. Optimum, proceeding without a lawyer, had not identified any accused products by name, model, or manufacturer despite repeated requests from Staff, and the ALJ found it had not proven infringement of claims 1 and 12-14 of the '511 patent or claims 1 and 3 of the '260 patent because it relied on practicing the standards themselves rather than identifying specific infringing products. Optimum also abandoned its infringement theories under the IEEE EPON and 10G-EPON standards by not addressing them in its pre-hearing brief, under a ground rule requiring parties to detail all contentions before the hearing.

The ALJ also found that Optimum had not satisfied either prong of the domestic industry requirement: the technical prong failed because Optimum did not identify specific domestic products practicing the claims, and the economic prong failed because EPB did not become a licensee until June 12, 2024 -- after the complaint was filed -- and Optimum's earlier authorization letter to EPB was not a license, and in any event Optimum offered no quantitative analysis of EPB's investment. The ALJ further found the importation requirement unsatisfied and found that the Staff had not challenged validity, so none of the asserted claims was shown invalid. The ALJ found separately that post-institution assignments of the patents -- from Optimum to Sandstrom and back -- made Optimum's standing questionable, and that the Commission lacked statutory authority because Optimum was not shown to own or exclusively license the patents; the ALJ recommended no exclusion or cease-and-desist orders and a 0% bond.

On March 11, 2025, the Commission determined to review the final ID in its entirety. After receiving public interest submissions -- one supporting a general exclusion order and one from Xenogenic opposing it -- the Commission, in a notice with a vote taken April 25, 2025, affirmed the ALJ's findings that Optimum had not satisfied the importation requirement, had not shown infringement of the asserted claims of either patent, and had not satisfied the domestic industry requirement. The Commission struck the ALJ's statement that it lacked statutory authority due to Optimum's ownership status, taking no position on the ownership issue itself. The Commission found no violation of Section 337 and terminated the investigation, issuing no exclusion order and no cease and desist order.

summary.headline: Optimum Communications Services, Inc. accused three Chinese manufacturers (Hangzhou Softel Optic, Hangzhou DAYTAI Network Technologies, and Hangzhou Sumlo Industrial) of importing passive optical network (OLT and ONU/ONT) equipment that infringed two of its patents, and the Commission ultimately found no violation of Section 337 and terminated the investigation.

rulings.text: On May 9, 2024, all three named respondents -- Softel, DAYTAI, and Sumlo -- were found in default by initial determination for failing to respond to the complaint, after an earlier initial determination on this point issued April 10, 2024.

Xenogenic Development LLC moved to intervene, claiming ownership of the asserted patents. The ALJ granted Xenogenic limited intervenor status to address ownership issues in the event of Commission review, without deciding ownership itself at that stage.

standing.text: The investigation is terminated. All three named respondents were found in default earlier in the case rather than settling or consenting. The Commission found no violation of Section 337 as to any asserted claim of the '511 patent or the '260 patent, affirming the ALJ's findings of no infringement, no domestic industry, and no importation, while declining to adopt the ALJ's separate finding on the Commission's statutory authority tied to patent ownership. No exclusion order or cease and desist order is in force, and no bond applies, as the case ended without any remedy.
